title: Anchor e2e-app check timed out starting its server on 4 branches
summary: The anchor `e2e-app` PR check failed on four branches between 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-09 before any browser test ran: Playwright stopped waiting for the disposable e2e server after its 180 s `webServer` timeout. That budget covers two serial phases: the backend (Postgres plus `go build ./cmd`) and `vite build`. On green runs the backend phase alone took 33 to 150 s; on the 16:18Z run it took 165 s, leaving 15 s for a frontend build that needs about 20 to 40 s. Each failure was green on rerun, so it read as a flake. The fix raises the budget to 420 s and logs the backend phase time.

impact.text: CI only. Four PR branches got a red required e2e check with no test failure and needed a manual rerun; no deploy or customer impact.

numbers.label: branches with a red e2e-app check

trigger: On `feat/search-db-adopt` the backend phase of `serve-e2e-full.mjs` took 165 s, and `vite build` could not finish inside the remaining 15 s.
detection: The echopoint-investigation routine logged the first two failures (anchor#323 branch, 2026-11-04) as an open ledger row and waited for a second branch; it found three more on 2026-11-09 by grepping job logs for `Timed out waiting 180000ms`. No CI signal separates a startup timeout from a test failure, so authors saw a generic red check and reran.
resolution: Each affected run went green on rerun. anchor PR (this postmortem) raises the `webServer` timeout in `playwright.app.config.ts` to 420 s and prints `Anchor backend ready in … ms` so the next budget question has data.

events.label: First timeout, anchor#323 branch (green on rerun)
Routine logs it as an open ledger row, waits for a 2nd branch
`vite build` starts after a 165 s backend phase
Next run on the branch is green
Routine finds the second-branch timeouts in job logs
Fix PR opened: 420 s budget + backend phase log

whys.problem: Four anchor PR branches got a red required `e2e-app` check without a failing test and had to be rerun.

because.text: Playwright gave up waiting for the e2e server: `Timed out waiting 180000ms from config.webServer`.
because.evidence: [run 42653368599](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/anchor/actions/runs/42653368599) log line at 16:22:32Z; same line in the other three failed runs

because.text: The backend phase took 165 s, leaving 15 s for `vite build`, which needs about 20 to 40 s.
Backend start (Postgres compose up + `go build ./cmd`) varies from 33 to 150 s on green runs, with the Go build cache.
because.evidence: 14 green runs on 2026-11-09: gap from `test:e2e:verify` to `vite build` 33 s to 150 s (`scripts/e2e-runtime.mjs` runs `go build` before starting Anchor)

because.text: One fixed 180 s budget, sized from typical runs, covers two serial phases whose worst case was never measured.
It recurred for six days across four branches before anyone changed the budget.
Each failure was green on rerun and looked like a generic red check, so it was treated as a flake.
because.evidence: anchor#323 runs 2 of 3 red then green (ledger row `ci:github:anchor:e2e-app`); later branches green on their next push

because.text: Startup logs no per-phase time and CI does not flag a startup timeout apart from a test failure, so the shrinking margin was invisible.

contributing: Branches that touch many Go packages (codegen migrations, search refactor) recompile most of `./cmd`, the slow end of the backend range.
The e2e job timeout is 15 min, so the 180 s startup budget was far tighter than the job needed.

well: The failing log kept enough timestamps to split the 180 s into its two phases after the fact.
wrong: A red-then-green check was logged and left open for six days instead of measured once.
lucky: The timeouts hit PR checks only; the e2e suite does not gate deploys, so nothing was held from prod.

actions.what: Raise the `webServer` timeout in `playwright.app.config.ts` from 180 s to 420 s, with the measured range in a comment
`serve-e2e-full.mjs` prints `Anchor backend ready in … ms` before the frontend build; e2e guide line on sizing the budget
Report a webServer startup timeout as its own annotation in `run-e2e-affected.mjs`, so it is not read as a test failure
Build the backend and the frontend in parallel in `serve-e2e-full.mjs` (startup becomes the max of the two phases, not the sum)

messaging.internal: anchor e2e-app red checks with `Timed out waiting 180000ms from config.webServer` were a startup budget, not flaky tests: backend build + frontend build ran serially inside 180 s. Budget raised to 420 s; the log now prints the backend phase time.
